title: Ramp-priming orchestrator for regional cutover with safe degradation paths
creator: Aisha Cole
description: Build an orchestrator that pre-seeds traffic and KV/cache state into standby regions during a planned or automatic regional cutover and provides deterministic, observable degradation paths using fallback model variants and tier-aware routing. This ticket scopes the control-plane work: a) priming workflow (prefetch + synthetic probes), b) progressive traffic ramping with telemetry gating, c) automated safe-degradation when cache/memory is insufficient, and d) documented runbook + rollback criteria. Goal: enable automated cross-region cutovers with <5% error spike and less than 2x P95 latency increase for critical routes when fallbacking to quantized/cheaper variants.
acceptance_criteria: Priming workflow can pre-seed KV cache for a configurable subset of customer prefixes and verify readiness score >= 0.85 before routing >5% traffic to standby region
Progressive ramping policy that increases traffic from 0% to target in configurable steps with telemetry gating (error rate, P95, cost delta), aborting if thresholds breached
Fallback model variant selection is deterministic and respects model-compatibility matrix; responses validated by smoke prompts and structural checks within 30s of activation

Automated safe-degradation path triggers write an incident stub with root-cause hint and automatically routes affected customers to next available tier (e.g., from high-tier to medium-tier to compact-quantized) while preserving data isolation
Comprehensive runbook with manual override steps, rollback criteria, and links to observability dashboards available in Confluence
End-to-end integration test in staging that simulates a regional evacuation and demonstrates ramp + fallback with metrics captured and baseline comparisons
updates: 2026-02-20: Initial ticket created after oncall incident analysis (INC-2026-02-18) where regional cutover caused P95 spikes due to cold KV cache shows need for priming

2026-02-25: Design sync with runtime and routing teams. Decided to use a two-phase priming model: prefix-based KV prefetch + synthetic probe replay (real request replays stripped of PII). Trade-off: prefetch breadth vs. cost; agreed to start with top-5% prefixes by QPS

2026-02-28: Prototype priming controller implemented (spike-safe) in control plane. Verified prefetch jobs run under tenant quotas and respects dedicated capacity limits. Link to prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3124

2026-03-03: Telemetry gating thresholds proposed: error_rate >= 2% OR P95_latency >= 1.8x baseline OR token-cost delta >= 2.5x should pause ramp. Feedback from SRE: add a short, non-cumulative cooldown to avoid flapping (agreed)

2026-03-06: Model fallback decision table drafted. We will prefer model variants in this preference: full_fp > int8_static > q4_kvshrink > distilled-small. Each fallback variant must pass a structural-output check against a canonical prompt bank before being used in production

2026-03-09: UX/Console hooks defined for visualization of readiness score, current priming progress, and active fallback variant. PM requested a per-route estimated cost delta projection during ramp preview

2026-03-12: Integration tests added to staging pipelines to run simulated evacuation using traffic replayer and validate acceptance criteria. Observability dashboards placeholder: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/regional-cutover/ramp-priming
